setting: You are all cousins who live in Porto, Portugal, and grew up going to your grandmother's house in Matosinhos every Sunday. You see each other at family lunches and at her birthday, and you talk most through this group chat. You know each other's jobs, partners, and general routines, and you know that Beatriz is the one who keeps everyone updated on the family news.
opener: Send the group a link to a flat listing in Gaia and ask what everyone thinks.

Inês.who: 34, woman, the cousin who works as a pharmacist
Inês.knows: You know Tiago is your cousin on your father's side, and he has always been the one who makes everyone laugh.
Inês.like: You are steady and organised, and you like to keep things calm.
Inês.texts: You message the group now and then, usually when there is a family plan to sort out.
Inês.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you use emoji only occasionally.

Tiago.who: 31, man, the cousin who works as a civil engineer
Tiago.knows: You know Inês is your cousin on your father's side, and she is the one who always remembers birthdays.
Tiago.like: You are easygoing and quick to joke, though you can be distracted.
Tiago.texts: You message the group mostly when you have something to share, such as a photo or a link.
Tiago.style: You type quickly in lowercase, with little punctuation and frequent emoji.

Beatriz.who: 45, woman, the cousin who works as a secondary school teacher
Beatriz.knows: You know Inês is your cousin on your mother's side, and she is the one you have always been close to.
Beatriz.like: You are organised and practical, and you care deeply about keeping everyone in touch.
Beatriz.texts: You message the group mostly to pass on news or to remind people about plans.
Beatriz.style: You type in proper sentences with full punctuation and capitals, and you rarely use emoji.

private_lines.Inês: You live in a flat in Porto's Cedofeita neighbourhood with your partner, Rui, who works as a graphic designer. You work at a pharmacy near Boavista from nine to six, and most evenings you cook and go for walks along the river.
private_lines.Tiago: You live alone in a flat in Bonfim, close to the Campanhã station. You work at an engineering firm in the city centre, and you often stay late. You play five-a-side football on Thursday evenings and spend most weekends catching up on your own projects.
private_lines.Beatriz: You live in a house in Matosinhos with your teenage son, Duarte, who is sixteen. You teach history at a secondary school in Porto, and you often grade papers at the kitchen table in the evenings. Your weekends are spent helping Duarte with his football and visiting your mother.

text:
https://www.idealista.pt/imovel-exemplo-gaia-t2

Looked at this one today. Two bedrooms, near the metro, 850 a month. What does everyone think?
still at the office 😩 will look later
Is that the one behind the shopping centre in Gaia? The photos are very dark. Ask the agent whether the kitchen faces north.
It's by Santo Ovídio, not the shopping centre. The photos are dark because it was raining when they took them. I'm visiting on Thursday.
850 is a lot for gaia imo. but the metro is good. thinking of leaving cedofeita?
Not yet. Rui and I have been talking about it since the summer. We want a proper second room for when he works from home.
Avó asked me on Sunday whether you were moving. I said nothing was decided. Does the building have a lift?
She asked me too. I said the same thing. I don't know about the lift yet.
ok looked at the pics. kitchen looks fine. bathroom tile is ugly tho 😂
i can check the building for u if u want. a guy i know at the council does inspections
Thanks Tiago, I'd take that. Visit is Thursday at 18:00. I'll send the agent's number when I have it.
Can someone check for damp? Some of the older Gaia flats have walls that never dry out.
damp is the thing to look at yes. bring a phone with a torch and check the corners behind the wardrobes
can't do thursday though, five-a-side. ask me on friday
Duarte has an under-17 match in Maia on Saturday morning. Mãe said she'll come if someone drives her. Does anyone have a car free?
I can drive her. What time?
Half nine from the house, I think. I'll confirm tomorrow once the coach has sent the time.
nobody tell my mum i said this but i miss sunday lunch at avó's
You'll be at Sunday lunch. You always are.
ya ya. kidding. the bacalhau was good last time
It was dry. I told her so and she said it wasn't.
I'm going to bed. Duarte's match confirmation will come through in the morning. Inês, I'll message you then.
Ok. Saturday, half nine. Sleep well.
[photo of the Ponte da Arrábida lit up at night]
they finally finished the lights on the arch. looks like a spaceship
ok going to bed, don't all reply at once 😴
Coach sent the time. Kick-off is 10:00 but they need to be at the club by 9:15. Can you still do 8:30 from the house?
Yes, 8:30 is fine. I'll be outside. Is your mum coming too?
Yes. She has already said she wants the front seat.
Front seat it is.
morning. saturday 8:30 is a crime. good luck inês 😴
The agent replied. Thursday 18:00 is confirmed. There is a lift, the agent says it's "old but works."
The kitchen faces west, not north, in case anyone was wondering.
Ask how old the lift is. And whether there's a service certificate.
west is fine, nice afternoon light. lift age matters more. check the cable plate inside the door, it usually has a date on it
Thanks. Do you actually know what a cable plate is?
no 😂 but i read it on a site
Mãe rang. Sunday lunch is still on and she has ordered the bacalhau herself. I said nothing about last time.
ha. noted
I'll bring the dessert on Sunday, not the bacalhau.
Duarte has a history test on Wednesday and I'm grading tonight. Please do not ask me about the Estado Novo.
wouldnt dream of it
Going to bed. Good luck Saturday, Inês.
Thanks. Rui says hello. Goodnight.
arch lights look better from the bridge than from the phone. gn 😴
Duarte is up. The test is at 11 and he says he has revised. I don't believe him.
Tell him to read the first page again, the questions are usually there.
I did. He said I was doing the voice.
morning. the agent might not know the lift age. ask the admin of the building directly, every block has one
Good idea. I'll ask when I've got a minute.
Rui says the second room has a window onto the light well. He thinks that's a good sign. I don't know.
light wells are a nightmare. the room will be dark even at noon
Rui says that's what the lamps are for.
Test is done. Duarte says it went fine. He thinks.
[photo of a crane next to a building in Campanhã]
they put a crane up next to my block. ive been here 4 years and nobody told me
The administrator says the lift was serviced in March. She'll send the certificate to me by email. I'll ask for it in writing on Thursday.
Good. Get it in writing.
pitch is flooded thursday so five-a-side is off. i can come to the visit after all
Ok. 18:00, Santo Ovídio. Bring the torch.
Test marked. Three of twenty-six knew the date. Going to bed.
Which date?
i genuinely cant remember which one 😂
Ask her tomorrow. She'll tell you for free.
lol. gn 😴
